passages.heading: **The standard “Good morning”: *Bonjour***
passages.text:
### **The standard “Good morning”: *Bonjour***

*Bonjour*

If you break it down, *Bonjour*, the French go-to greeting, means “good” (*bon*) and “day” (*jour*). That’s why it works perfectly for “Good morning”. When you think about it, it’s maybe *even better* than “Good morning”, since you’re wishing someone an entire good day.

*Bonjour* first thing in the morning might seem weirdly formal to you at first. I know that was the case for me. But I can tell you firsthand that it’s what French people really do say to each other. For instance, when we’re not just nodding to each other in a tired fog, my husband will greet me with *Bonjour*.

So this is the best French “Good morning” for formal or informal occasions and the first greeting we teach in our conversational French course.

passages.heading: Other common ways to say good morning in French
passages.text:
### Other common ways to say good morning in French

There are a lot of other ways to say good morning in French, including:

- *Bonjour mon amour* - Good morning, my love/ good morning love
- *Bonjour, comment allez-vous?* - Good morning, how are you? (formal)

passages.heading: **Do the French say “Good morning” to each other?**
passages.text:
## **Do the French say “Good morning” to each other?**

Even though French people don’t have a specific phrase for “Good morning”, it’s certainly normal to greet family, friends, roommates, coworkers, etc. in the morning. They just usually say *Bonjour*.

Of course, when it comes to the people you live with, if you’re not a “morning person”, you may not say much of anything. But in general, remember that the French do tend to be polite and greet each other, so even a friendly nod or trying to grumble out one of the ways to say “good morning” in French is a good idea!

Saying “Good morning” in French may not be as evident as you were expecting, but now you know several ways to go about it. In French, the word for good morning is: *bonjour*. In French culture, it is very important to greet those around you in the morning with a polite *bonjour*. passages.heading: Parents and grand parents
passages.text:
## Parents and grand parents

In French culture, it’s is common for kids to follow *bonjour* in the morning with *maman* (mom) and *papa* (dad). The same goes for addressing grand parents.

- *Bonjour, maman* good morning, mom
- *Bonjour, papa* good morning dad
- *Bonjour, mamie* good morning, grandma
- *Bonjour, papie* good morning, grandpa

bonjour is the most common and standard way to say "Good Morning" in French. It is used when seeing someone for the first time in the morning. While it is used to mean "good morning," it literally translates to "good day" and serves as the standard way to say "hello" during daylight hours.

passages.heading: What is good morning in French?
passages.text:
## What is good morning in French?

The standard way to say good morning in French is *bonjour* (good day), which covers everything from sunrise until roughly 5 PM. Be careful with *bonne matinée* (have a good morning), it looks like a greeting, but it is actually a farewell used before noon.

- 
*bonjour* (good day): Used as the standard greeting from morning until late afternoon
- 
*bonne matinée* (have a good morning): Said only when saying goodbye before noon

When in doubt, new learners should default to *bonjour*: it’s warm, respectful, and welcome almost anywhere.

passages.heading: *Bonjour* (good day)
passages.text:
### *Bonjour* (good day)

*Bonjour* pairs *bon* (good) with *jour* (day), and it fits every morning setting from bakeries to boardrooms. French speakers reach for it right up until *bonsoir* (good evening) takes over in the late afternoon. Quick example: *Bonjour, comment allez-vous?* (Good morning, how are you?).

passages.heading: Quick Answer
passages.text:
## Quick Answer

French does not have a direct translation for 'good morning.' The standard greeting is 'Bonjour' (bohn-ZHOOR), which means 'good day' and covers both morning and afternoon. In Québec, you may hear 'Bon matin' (a calque from English) but it is considered non-standard in Metropolitan French. Native speakers also use morning-specific expressions like 'Bien dormi ?' (sleep well?), 'Bonne matinée' (have a good morning), and 'Ça va ce matin ?' (how's it going this morning?).

passages.text: Whether you’re jet-setting to Europe or hanging out with a French-speaking friend, it’s handy to have the French word for “good morning” stashed somewhere in your mental phrasebook. We’ve got you covered with plenty of friendly, personalized greetings you can use each morning, along with some physical greetings that are common in French culture. In just a few minutes, you’ll be a pro at greeting anyone and everyone in the language of love.

passages.text:

**"Bonjour" *(bohn-zhoor)* is how you say “good morning” in most French-speaking countries.***Bonjour* is a pretty versatile greeting—it can mean “hello,” “good morning,” or “good day.” You can even use it later in the day to say “good afternoon.”<sup>[1]</sup>
  - In France, people always say *bonjour* to greet other people, even if the situation is a little unconventional. For instance, you’d said “bonjour” when entering a crowded elevator.<sup>[2]</sup>
  - If you’re exiting the conversation, offer a friendly *bonne matinée* (buhn meh-tee-nay) or*bonne journée* (buhn-zhoor-nay), which mean “have a good morning” or “have a good day,” respectively.<sup>[3]</sup>

passages.heading: About This Article
passages.text:
## About This Article

The most common way to say "good morning" in French is "bonjour," which works well in any social setting. When you're greeting your close friends in the morning, feel free to switch to "salut," which is very informal and similar to "hi" or "hey" in English. If you would like to say "good morning" to a married woman, say "bonjour madame." To say "good morning" to an unmarried woman, you can say "bonjour mademoiselle," which is like saying "Good morning, miss!" in English. You could also say "bonjour monsieur" to say "Good morning, sir!" If you want to address a crowd, say "bonjour à tous," meaning "Good morning, everyone!" To learn about other greetings in French, read on!
